subject: general
question: The marked price of a TV is ₹50,000. The difference between a discount of 30% and two successive discounts of 25% and 6% on this deal is:
solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Equivalent percentage of successive discounts 25% and 6% = 25 + 6 − (25 × 6)/100 = 29.5% Difference between 30% single discount and 29.5% successive discount = 30% − 29.5% = 0.5% Difference in amount = 0.5% of ₹50,000 ⇒ (0.5/100) × 50000 = ₹250 **∴ The correct answer is ₹250.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** **Given:** Marked Price (MP) = ₹50,000 Discount 1 = 30% Successive Discounts = 25% and 6% **Formula Used:** Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − Discount%/100) MP ₹50,000 • Single Discount -30% SP 1 ₹35,000 • Diff = ₹250 MP ₹50,000 • -25% ₹37,500 • -6% SP 2 ₹35,250 **Calculations:** **Case 1 (Single discount of 30%):** ⇒ SP₁ = 50000 × (1 − 30/100) = 50000 × 0.70 = ₹35,000 **Case 2 (Successive discounts of 25% and 6%):** ⇒ SP₂ = 50000 × (1 − 25/100) × (1 − 6/100) ⇒ SP₂ = 50000 × 0.75 × 0.94 ⇒ SP₂ = 37500 × 0.94 = ₹35,250 **Difference:** The difference in discounts is identical to the difference in Selling Prices. ⇒ Difference = SP₂ − SP₁ ⇒ Difference = 35250 − 35000 = ₹250 **∴ The correct answer is ₹250.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** Successive Discounts When a discount is given on the previously discounted price, it is called a successive discount. The equivalent discount of D₁% and D₂% is given by the formula: [D₁ + D₂ − (D₁ × D₂)/100]%. Marked Price (MP) It is the label price of an article. Any discount offered by a merchant is always calculated on the Marked Price, not on the Cost Price. Single Discount vs Successive Discount A single flat discount equal to the sum of successive discount percentages is always greater than the successive discount combined. For example, a flat 30% discount is always more beneficial to a buyer than successive discounts of 25% and 5%. 179:T128c,
